## Goal

Require a second factor to use the administration area, by whichever route decision D-013 settles on.

## Context

Only a password protects the administration area today, and anyone who gets in can read every customer and accounting record. Request-rate limits and a short session token reduce the exposure but do not remove it. The customer side has a second factor; the administration side does not. SC-019 delivers the comparison and the owner's decision in D-013; this package implements it. Details are in the owner's private tracker.

## Scope

- Implement the option D-013 settles on. Do not start before that entry says Accepted.
- Cover every administrator entry point, not only the panel: the admin API routes, any direct sign-in path, and recovery.
- A documented recovery procedure for a lost factor that does not reduce to turning the factor off.
- `docs/SECURITY.md` and `docs/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md` record what is enforced and how it is verified.

## Out of scope

- Customer two-factor behaviour (SC-021).
- Choosing the approach: that is D-013, owner-decided.
- Buying a service the owner has not approved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every administrator entry point requires the factor, shown one by one in the PR, including the admin API routes and recovery.
- [ ] A session that authenticated before the factor was enforced cannot continue without it.
- [ ] The recovery procedure has been exercised once on staging and recorded.
- [ ] A manual attempt to reach the panel with a correct password and no factor fails, with the real output pasted.
- [ ] Independent review approves.

## Required tests

- Tests at every entry point.
- A manual staging walkthrough of sign-in, failure and recovery, recorded on the issue.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-019

## Priority

P1 · Phase A

## Agent

Claude Code
